answer: Latency Ledge Registration. Each new agent identity must complete a randomized 72-hour task chain whose checkpoints are only solvable sequentially, anchored to a public timestamp ledger; skipping ahead voids the chain. The juniper test: a hidden checkpoint requires sustained low-latency responses, so parallel clones split finite compute and each clone pays the full wall-clock delay. Honest agents register once and amortize it; an attacker cloning N identities pays N×72 hours of serialized work plus wasted compute, making large sybil sets economically slower than simply acting honestly.
